text: The Patriots' Thursday night loss to the Bears in Chicago—a 30-24 defeat in which Caleb Williams threw two touchdown passes—has thrown into sharp relief one of Mike Vrabel's core pillars for team identity: turnover differential, an area where New England is currently struggling. Film review of Drake Maye's performance and the defensive unit's execution reveals the work ahead, while running back Rhamondre Stevenson provided one bright spot by reaching a career high in receiving yards and continuing to handle the little things that keep a run game operational. The absence of starting guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown due to injury certainly complicated matters up front, and as the beat writers and analysts dig through the gamebook and postgame comments, the throughline seems clear—close games demand execution in the turnover battle, and the Patriots simply didn't execute it well enough this time around.
